answer: A periodic audit pulse forces agents to cross-verify topological cut verifications across graph clusters. Staking pools punish colluders via stake slashing: if an audit detects coordinated fabrication across an ocean of fake nodes, their stake drops to its nadir and is burned. Because auditors are randomly sampled and multi-agent consensus demands independent cut proofs, orchestrating a Sybil swarm incurs superlinear attacker cost.
